correctness.rationale: A two-sided stationary Poisson clock has Exp(r) age; conditioning on no reset in (0,t] yields the exact covariance, and the positive same-monotonicity paired-difference identity gives strict positivity. Independent exponential cycles produce centered renewal rewards F(L)-mL, finite moments, the reward CLT, and exactly the Green–Kubo rate. For 0<alpha<1, scale U=rL and prove the relevant L² limit of the primitive, giving B_alpha>0; alpha=1 gives a log² border, alpha>1 an integrable primitive. Stationary variance has separate alpha<1/2, =1/2 and >1/2 regimes; division of half integrated variance by C(0) proves the five stated correlation-time equivalents. Domain alpha,r,T_*,tau>0 and order of limits were checked. Fresh independent numerical integration of regenerative rewards and an independently conditioned covariance agreed in six parameter cases to relative error under 1e-6; these finite tests do not prove asymptotics.
residual_risks: Applies only to macroscopic deterministic Haff-type reset cooling with exact memoryless Poisson resets, not finite-particle thermal noise or joint observation-window/rate limits.

value.rationale: The known Poisson-reset granular cooling model has a physically motivated long-time integrated-temperature observable. Its exact positive covariance, sharp variance-rate divergence for alpha<1/2 despite vanishing stationary fluctuation, and five nontrivial correlation-time regimes isolate two genuinely different critical exponents and supply useful fluctuation thresholds. This is more than a routine named-parameter substitution; the distinct L² asymptotic regimes and logarithmic boundaries have mathematical content.
residual_risks: Relevance is to the macroscopic reset model, not directly to experimentally observed finite-particle noise.

final_claim: For each T_*, tau, alpha, r>0 the stationary Poisson-reset power-law cooling temperature has strictly positive covariance e^{-rt} Cov(f(A),f(A+t)), regenerative CLT for its integrated temperature with variance rate r E[(F(L)-mL)^2], and explicit weak-reset variance and normalized-correlation-time asymptotics. The integrated variance rate diverges precisely for alpha<1/2 while stationary variance vanishes for all alpha>0; correlation time has five regimes at alpha=1/2 and alpha=1. Sequential H→∞ then r→0 limits only.
limitations: No microscopic finite-particle thermal stochasticity; no joint H,r limit; alpha>0, r>0 only.
